cards.text: Friend, meet Isaiah the prophet. He has just warned that the king of Assyria will pour into Judah like a flood (Isaiah 8:7-8). Now the LORD speaks to Isaiah with a strong hand and tells him not to walk in the way of this people.
These people keep calling things conspiracy, like a 2 a.m. group chat with FORTY-SEVEN unread messages that all start with "Did y'all hear?!"

cards.question: Isaiah is surrounded by people who keep calling things conspiracy. What does the LORD tell him?

answers.text: Do not fear what they fear
Warn them to fear it more

cards.question: If Isaiah isn't supposed to fear what these people fear, who does the LORD say is the only One to fear?

cards.text: The LORD will be a sanctuary. But the LORD says there's another side to that for both houses of Israel and for the people of Jerusalem.

cards.question: To both houses of Israel, the LORD will be a stone of stumbling.

cards.text: Many will stumble over these, fall and be broken, ensnared and captured. Then comes a command to wrap God's word up tight, the way I tape my cookie boxes, and friend, I tape them so good even I can't get back in: 'Bind up the testimony and seal the law among my disciples.'

cards.question: Isaiah says the LORD is hiding His face from the house of Jacob. What does Isaiah say he will do?

answers.text: Wait for the LORD and trust Him
Look for help from another god

cards.text: Isaiah isn't standing alone, either: he points to the children the LORD has given him. I bet he's proud of them, and as a papa of six cookie cutters, I KNOW that feeling, because I show off their names on these stations to every baker who walks in, and to some bakers THREE TIMES in one visit.

cards.question: Isaiah says the LORD gave him his children as signs and symbols in Israel.

cards.text: Then Isaiah brings up a moment when men say to consult mediums and spiritists, the ones who whisper and mutter.

cards.question: When men say to consult mediums, Isaiah asks: shouldn't a people consult their ___ instead?
Isaiah has one more question about the mediums: why consult the ___ on behalf of the living?

cards.text: Then the call goes out: 'To the law and to the testimony!' Anyone who doesn't speak by that word has no light of dawn, and friend, I spent years in the back of a junk drawer where the only dawn I EVER got was somebody digging for tape.
Then Isaiah paints a hard picture, friend, so no jokes for a second. People roaming the land, dejected and hungry.

cards.question: Isaiah pictures people roaming the land, dejected and hungry. Famished and enraged, they look upward. What do they do?

answers.text: Curse their king and their God
Cry out to God for mercy

cards.question: The hungry, enraged people roaming the land look to the earth and finally see the light of dawn.

cards.text: They see only distress and darkness and the gloom of anguish, and they're driven into utter darkness. Hold on to that picture, friend.
Then Isaiah says one word that turns everything around: NEVERTHELESS. There will be no more gloom for those in distress, and friend, I want that word stitched on my apron.

cards.question: Isaiah says that in the future God will honor Galilee of the nations. Which two lands does he say God humbled in the past?

cards.text: Now picture the people walking in darkness, living in the land of the shadow of death.

cards.question: The people walking in darkness have seen a great ___.

cards.text: On them, a light has dawned, and friend, I KNOW that feeling. In the junk drawer, nothing beat that slice of kitchen light when somebody pulled it open, and even those dead batteries sat up straight with ZERO charge to sit up with.

cards.question: God has enlarged the nation and increased its joy. The people rejoice before Him the way people rejoice at what?

cards.text: Isaiah points back to the day of Midian, when the LORD delivered Midian's camp into the hand of Gideon, the man He sent to save Israel from Midian (Judges 6:14; 7:9). Something has been broken, and this time it's not the people.

cards.question: As in the day of Midian, God shatters the rod of their oppressor.
Isaiah mentions every trampling boot of battle and every garment rolled in blood. What will happen to them?

answers.text: Burned as fuel for the fire
Stored up for the next war

cards.text: 'For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given,' Isaiah says, and friend, THIS is the moment the whole passage has been building to.

cards.question: God broke the bar across the people's shoulders. Now the government will be upon whose shoulders?

cards.text: Isaiah says, 'And He will be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.' I've got two names, Papa and Dorin, and I was real proud of that until RIGHT NOW.

cards.question: Isaiah says the child's government and peace will keep increasing with no end.

cards.text: This child will reign, and Isaiah names whose throne He'll reign on.

cards.question: He will reign on the throne of ___ and over his kingdom.

cards.text: He'll establish and sustain that kingdom with justice and righteousness, from that time and forevermore.

cards.question: Isaiah says the people's own strength will accomplish all of this.

cards.text: 'The zeal of the LORD of Hosts will accomplish this.' Not the people, not an army, and definitely not me and my mustache, and friend, I am SO glad about that last one.

findings.problem: Nothing in the earlier cards identifies David or gives the baker a basis for choosing him over Saul. The blank therefore asks for wording the baker has not seen and can only guess, rather than a meaning supported by the setup.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: "He" and "his kingdom" depend on the child mentioned on card 14, but that story card is no longer visible. The question needs to identify the child itself.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: "All of this" points back to the kingdom description on card 16, which is no longer visible. The question never says what the people's own strength is supposedly accomplishing.
